extracted.intended_audience: federal agency officials, General Services Administration staff, Congressional committees, and other officials responsible for establishing, managing, or overseeing federal advisory committees
extracted.subtask_description: Rules and standards from the Federal Advisory Committee Act governing creation, composition, operation, transparency, recordkeeping, funding, review, renewal/termination, and use of advisory committees and their products. Intended to guide agencies, the GSA Administrator, and Congress in compliant committee management.

rubrics_metrics.name: Establishment authorization
rubrics_metrics.description: No advisory committee shall be established unless such establishment is (1) specifically authorized by statute or by the President; or (2) determined as a matter of formal record, by the head of the agency involved after consultation with the Administrator, with timely notice published in the Federal Register, to be in the public interest in connection with the performance of duties imposed on that agency by law.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Establishment must be based on explicit statutory/Presidential authority or a formal agency determination with Federal Register notice.

rubrics_metrics.name: Advisory-only function
rubrics_metrics.description: Unless otherwise specifically provided by statute or Presidential directive, advisory committees shall be utilized solely for advisory functions. Determinations of action to be taken and policy to be expressed with respect to matters upon which an advisory committee reports or makes recommendations shall be made solely by the President or an officer of the Federal Government.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Advisory committees cannot exercise decision-making or policy-determining authority unless statute specifically grants such authority; agencies/officers retain final decision.

rubrics_metrics.name: Charter requirement and timing
rubrics_metrics.description: No advisory committee shall meet or take any action until an advisory committee charter has been filed with (1) the Administrator, in the case of Presidential advisory committees, or (2) with the head of the agency to whom any advisory committee reports and with the standing committees of the Senate and of the House of Representatives having legislative jurisdiction of such agency.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Filing the charter is a prerequisite to meetings or committee actions (except preparation/filing of charter).

rubrics_metrics.name: Charter contents — official designation
rubrics_metrics.description: The charter shall contain the committee's official designation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Charter must clearly state the committee's formal name.

rubrics_metrics.name: Charter contents — objectives and scope
rubrics_metrics.description: The charter shall contain the committee's objectives and the scope of its activity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Must define purpose and boundaries of committee work.

rubrics_metrics.name: Charter contents — period of time necessary
rubrics_metrics.description: The charter shall contain the period of time necessary for the committee to carry out its purposes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specify anticipated duration to justify establishment and future renewal/termination planning.

rubrics_metrics.name: Charter contents — reporting official/agency
rubrics_metrics.description: The charter shall contain the agency or official to whom the committee reports.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Identify the official/agency responsible for receiving committee advice and oversight.

rubrics_metrics.name: Charter contents — support agency
rubrics_metrics.description: The charter shall contain the agency responsible for providing the necessary support for the committee.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specify which agency provides administrative/logistical support.

rubrics_metrics.name: Charter contents — duties and authority
rubrics_metrics.description: The charter shall contain a description of the duties for which the committee is responsible, and, if such duties are not solely advisory, a specification of the authority for such functions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If committee has any non-advisory responsibilities, the charter must cite statutory or other authority for those duties.

rubrics_metrics.name: Charter contents — estimated costs
rubrics_metrics.description: The charter shall contain the estimated annual operating costs in dollars and man-years for such committee.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide budgetary estimates to inform oversight and appropriations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Charter contents — meeting frequency
rubrics_metrics.description: The charter shall contain the estimated number and frequency of committee meetings.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Helps plan resources and public notice obligations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Charter contents — termination date (if <2 years)
rubrics_metrics.description: The charter shall contain the committee's termination date, if less than two years from the date of the committee's establishment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Short-lived committees must specify an end date; otherwise statutory two-year rules apply.

rubrics_metrics.name: Charter filing date; Library of Congress copy
rubrics_metrics.description: The charter shall contain the date the charter is filed. A copy of any such charter shall also be furnished to the Library of Congress.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Track filing date and ensure public record availability via Library of Congress.

rubrics_metrics.name: Legislative content requirements for authorizing statutes
rubrics_metrics.description: Any legislation establishing, or authorizing the establishment of any advisory committee shall (1) contain a clearly defined purpose for the advisory committee; (2) require the membership of the advisory committee to be fairly balanced in terms of the points of view represented and the functions to be performed by the advisory committee; (3) contain appropriate provisions to assure that the advice and recommendations of the advisory committee will not be inappropriately influenced by the appointing authority or by any special interest, but will instead be the result of the advisory committee's independent judgment; (4) contain provisions dealing with authorization of appropriations, the date for submission of reports (if any), the duration of the advisory committee, and the publication of reports and other materials, to the extent that the standing committee determines the provisions of section 10 of this Act to be inadequate; and (5) contain provisions which will assure that the advisory committee will have adequate staff (either supplied by an agency or employed by it), will be provided adequate quarters, and will have funds available to meet its other necessary expenses.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authorizing legislation must address purpose, balance, independence, funding/reporting/duration, and administrative support.

rubrics_metrics.name: Fairly balanced membership
rubrics_metrics.description: Require the membership of the advisory committee to be fairly balanced in terms of the points of view represented and the functions to be performed by the advisory committee.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Membership selection must avoid dominance by one viewpoint or interest; 'fairly balanced' judged in context of functions to be performed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Independence from appointing authority and special interests
rubrics_metrics.description: Contain appropriate provisions to assure that the advice and recommendations of the advisory committee will not be inappropriately influenced by the appointing authority or by any special interest, but will instead be the result of the advisory committee's independent judgment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Statutes should include safeguards to protect independent committee judgment (conflict policies, disclosure, membership selection processes).

rubrics_metrics.name: Presidential response to public reports
rubrics_metrics.description: Within one year after a Presidential advisory committee has submitted a public report to the President, the President or his delegate shall make a report to the Congress stating either his proposals for action or his reasons for inaction, with respect to the recommendations contained in the public report.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensures accountability for presidential advisory committee recommendations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Administrator — Committee Management Secretariat and review duty
rubrics_metrics.description: The Administrator shall establish and maintain within the General Services Administration a Committee Management Secretariat, which shall be responsible for all matters relating to advisory committees. The Administrator shall, immediately after October 6, 1972, institute a comprehensive review of the activities and responsibilities of each advisory committee to determine whether such committee is carrying out its purpose, whether responsibilities should be revised, whether it should be merged with other advisory committees, or whether it should be abolished; and shall carry out similar reviews annually.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: GSA Administrator leads oversight, conducts initial and annual reviews, makes recommendations to the President, agency heads, or Congress.

rubrics_metrics.name: Administrator to prescribe administrative guidelines and management controls
rubrics_metrics.description: The Administrator shall prescribe administrative guidelines and management controls applicable to advisory committees, and, to the maximum extent feasible, provide advice, assistance, and guidance to advisory committees to improve their performance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: GSA issues consistent management guidance and supports committees to improve performance; agencies must consider agency head recommendations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Uniform pay and expense guidelines; GS-18 limit
rubrics_metrics.description: The Administrator, after study and consultation with the Director of the Office of Personnel Management, shall establish guidelines with respect to uniform fair rates of pay ... Such regulations shall provide that no member of any advisory committee or of the staff of any advisory committee shall receive compensation at a rate in excess of the rate specified for GS-18 of the General Schedule under section 5332 of Title 5, United States Code; such members, while engaged in performance of their duties away from their homes or regular places of business, may be allowed travel expenses, including per diem ...; members who are blind or deaf or otherwise qualify as handicapped individuals may be provided services pursuant to section 3102 of Title 5 while in performance of their advisory committee duties.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Sets maximum compensation, travel reimbursement, and accommodations for handicapped members; exceptions exist for individuals who are federal employees.

rubrics_metrics.name: Agency administrative guidelines and information maintenance
rubrics_metrics.description: Each agency head shall establish uniform administrative guidelines and management controls for advisory committees established by that agency, which shall be consistent with directives of the Administrator under section 7 and section 10. Each agency shall maintain systematic information on the nature, functions, and operations of each advisory committee within its jurisdiction.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Agency-level rules must align with GSA directives and keep systematic records about committees.

rubrics_metrics.name: Advisory Committee Management Officer designation and duties
rubrics_metrics.description: The head of each agency which has an advisory committee shall designate an Advisory Committee Management Officer who shall (1) exercise control and supervision over the establishment, procedures, and accomplishments of advisory committees established by that agency; (2) assemble and maintain the reports, records, and other papers of any such committee during its existence; and (3) carry out, on behalf of that agency, the provisions of section 552 of Title 5, United States Code, with respect to such reports, records, and other papers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Designate a single responsible official to supervise committees, maintain records, and handle public access under FOIA exemptions/requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Open meetings and public notice
rubrics_metrics.description: Each advisory committee meeting shall be open to the public. Except when the President determines otherwise for reasons of national security, timely notice of each such meeting shall be published in the Federal Register, and the Administrator shall prescribe regulations to provide for other types of public notice to insure that all interested persons are notified of such meeting prior thereto. Interested persons shall be permitted to attend, appear before, or file statements with any advisory committee, subject to such reasonable rules or regulations as the Administrator may prescribe.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Presumption of openness with FR notice and opportunity for public participation; Administrator may set reasonable rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: Public availability of committee records and documents
rubrics_metrics.description: Subject to section 552 of Title 5, the records, reports, transcripts, minutes, appendixes, working papers, drafts, studies, agenda, or other documents which were made available to or prepared for or by each advisory committee shall be available for public inspection and copying at a single location in the offices of the advisory committee or the agency to which the advisory committee reports until the advisory committee ceases to exist.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Single-location public access requirement; FOIA/exemption caveats apply.

rubrics_metrics.name: Minutes and certification
rubrics_metrics.description: Detailed minutes of each meeting of each advisory committee shall be kept and shall contain a record of the persons present, a complete and accurate description of matters discussed and conclusions reached, and copies of all reports received, issued, or approved by the advisory committee. The accuracy of all minutes shall be certified to by the chairman of the advisory committee.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Comprehensive, certified minutes required for transparency and accountability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Permitted closures and required written determinations
rubrics_metrics.description: Subsections (a)(1) and (a)(3) shall not apply to any portion of an advisory committee meeting where the President, or the head of the agency to which the advisory committee reports, determines that such portion of such meeting may be closed to the public in accordance with subsection (c) of section 552b of Title 5, United States Code. Any such determination shall be in writing and shall contain the reasons for such determination. If such a determination is made, the advisory committee shall issue a report at least annually setting forth a summary of its activities and such related matters as would be informative to the public consistent with the policy of section 552(b) of Title 5, United States Code.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Closures allowed only under statutory exemptions, with written justification; an annual public summary still required consistent with FOIA policy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Designation and role of Federal officer or employee at meetings
rubrics_metrics.description: There shall be designated an officer or employee of the Federal Government to chair or attend each meeting of each advisory committee. The officer or employee so designated is authorized, whenever he determines it to be in the public interest, to adjourn any such meeting. No advisory committee shall conduct any meeting in the absence of that officer or employee.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A designated federal official must attend/oversee meetings and has authority to adjourn.

rubrics_metrics.name: Meeting call/approval and agenda control
rubrics_metrics.description: Advisory committees shall not hold any meetings except at the call of, or with the advance approval of, a designated officer or employee of the Federal Government, and in the case of advisory committees (other than Presidential advisory committees), with an agenda approved by such officer or employee.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Meetings require federal oversight and preapproved agendas (except for Presidential committees where some differences apply).

rubrics_metrics.name: Availability of transcripts
rubrics_metrics.description: Except where prohibited by contractual agreements entered into prior to the effective date of this Act, agencies and advisory committees shall make available to any person, at actual cost of duplication, copies of transcripts of agency proceedings or advisory committee meetings.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Transcripts must generally be supplied upon request at cost, subject to prior contract prohibitions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Fiscal records, audits, and Comptroller General access
rubrics_metrics.description: Each agency shall keep records as will fully disclose the disposition of any funds which may be at the disposal of its advisory committees and the nature and extent of their activities. The General Services Administration, or such other agency as the President may designate, shall maintain financial records with respect to Presidential advisory committees. The Comptroller General of the United States, or any of his authorized representatives, shall have access, for the purpose of audit and examination, to any such records.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Maintain complete financial records and permit GAO/Comptroller General audit access.

rubrics_metrics.name: Agency support services responsibility
rubrics_metrics.description: Each agency shall be responsible for providing support services for each advisory committee established by or reporting to it unless the establishing authority provides otherwise. Where any such advisory committee reports to more than one agency, only one agency shall be responsible for support services at any one time. In the case of Presidential advisory committees, such services may be provided by the General Services Administration.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure a single responsible support provider for each committee to avoid duplication or gaps.

rubrics_metrics.name: Filing reports and depository at Library of Congress
rubrics_metrics.description: Subject to section 552 of Title 5, the Administrator shall provide for the filing with the Library of Congress of at least eight copies of each report made by every advisory committee and, where appropriate, background papers prepared by consultants. The Librarian of Congress shall establish a depository for such reports and papers where they shall be available to public inspection and use.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide public access via Library of Congress depository; file multiple copies for archiving and inspection.

rubrics_metrics.name: Termination and renewal timing rules
rubrics_metrics.description: Each advisory committee in existence on the effective date of this Act shall terminate not later than the expiration of the two-year period following such effective date unless renewed by the President or that officer or unless its duration is otherwise provided by law. Each advisory committee established after such effective date shall terminate not later than the expiration of the two-year period beginning on the date of its establishment unless renewed. Upon renewal, any such advisory committee shall file a charter in accordance with section 9(c). No advisory committee required under this subsection to file a charter shall take any action (other than preparation and filing of such charter) prior to the date on which such charter is filed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Default two-year lifespan with required renewal procedures and charter filing before activity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Restrictions on use of National Academy-created committees' work
rubrics_metrics.description: An agency may not use any advice or recommendation provided by the National Academy of Sciences or National Academy of Public Administration that was developed by use of a committee created by that academy under an agreement with an agency, unless (1) the committee was not subject to any actual management or control by an agency or an officer of the Federal Government; (2) in the case of a committee created after the FACA Amendments of 1997, the membership was appointed in accordance with subsection (b)(1); and (3) in developing the advice or recommendations, the academy complied with specified transparency and balance requirements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Conditions to accept Academy advice include independence from agency control and compliance with appointment, notice, and transparency rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: National Academy — public notice of appointees and opportunity for comment
rubrics_metrics.description: The Academy shall determine and provide public notice of the names and brief biographies of individuals that the Academy appoints or intends to appoint to serve on the committee. The Academy shall determine and provide a reasonable opportunity for the public to comment on such appointments before they are made or, if prior comment is impracticable, immediately following the appointments.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Promote transparency and public input on Academy committee appointments; disclose biographies and allow comment.

rubrics_metrics.name: National Academy — conflict of interest disclosure and fairness
rubrics_metrics.description: The Academy shall make its best efforts to ensure that (A) no individual appointed to serve on the committee has a conflict of interest that is relevant to the functions to be performed, unless such conflict is promptly and publicly disclosed and the Academy determines that the conflict is unavoidable, (B) the committee membership is fairly balanced as determined by the Academy to be appropriate for the functions to be performed, and (C) the final report of the Academy will be the result of the Academy's independent judgment. The Academy shall require that individuals appointed inform the Academy of the individual's conflicts of interest that are relevant to the functions to be performed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Require disclosure and mitigation of conflicts; ensure balance and independent final reports.

rubrics_metrics.name: National Academy — openness and materials availability for meetings
rubrics_metrics.description: The Academy shall determine and provide public notice of committee meetings that will be open to the public. The Academy shall ensure that meetings of the committee to gather data from individuals who are not officials, agents, or employees of the Academy are open to the public, unless the Academy determines that a meeting would disclose matters described in section 552(b) of Title 5. The Academy shall make available to the public, at reasonable charge if appropriate, written materials presented to the committee by individuals who are not officials, agents, or employees of the Academy, unless the Academy determines that making material available would disclose matters described in that section.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Data-gathering meetings should be open and materials from outside presenters generally made available, subject to FOIA exemptions.

rubrics_metrics.name: National Academy — summaries and final report availability
rubrics_metrics.description: The Academy shall make available to the public as soon as practicable, at reasonable charge if appropriate, a brief summary of any committee meeting that is not a data gathering meeting, unless the Academy determines that the summary would disclose matters described in section 552(b). The Academy shall make available to the public its final report, at reasonable charge if appropriate, unless the Academy determines that the report would disclose matters described in section 552(b). If so, the Academy shall make public an abbreviated version of the report that does not disclose those matters.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide summaries for non-data meetings and public access to final reports, with redacted/abbreviated versions if FOIA exemptions apply.

rubrics_metrics.name: National Academy — disclosure of principal reviewers
rubrics_metrics.description: After publication of the final report, the Academy shall make publicly available the names of the principal reviewers who reviewed the report in draft form and who are not officials, agents, or employees of the Academy.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Identify external principal reviewers to enhance transparency of the review process.

rubrics_metrics.name: Applicability exclusions
rubrics_metrics.description: The provisions of this Act shall not apply to any advisory committee established or utilized by (1) the Central Intelligence Agency; (2) the Federal Reserve System; or (3) the Office of the Director of National Intelligence, if the Director determines that for reasons of national security such advisory committee cannot comply with the requirements of this Act. Nothing in this Act shall be construed to apply to any local civic group whose primary function is that of rendering a public service with respect to a Federal program, or any State or local committee, council, board, commission, or similar group established to advise or make recommendations to State or local officials or agencies.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Statutory exclusions for certain agencies and local/state bodies; ODNI may exempt for national security reasons.

rubrics_metrics.name: Records retention and single-location public inspection until committee cessation
rubrics_metrics.description: Records and documents made available to or prepared for or by each advisory committee shall be available for public inspection and copying at a single location in the offices of the advisory committee or the agency to which the advisory committee reports until the advisory committee ceases to exist.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Maintain materials in a single public-access location for the life of the committee.
